title: Establish organizational ownership and scope
procedure: Reconcile organization, folders, project numbers, business owners, lifecycle state and billing inventory with the signed scope. Record separately projects visible to the collector and the expected population.
criterion: Every expected project has a disposition, owner and applicable control set; unexplained inventory gaps remain open.
falsification: Find one billing-linked or CMDB project absent from the asset export and investigate visibility before declaring it retired.
required_evidence: signed charter; independent project register; population reconciliation

title: Allocate shared responsibility
procedure: Map each material service to customer, Google and supplier duties, including data protection, IAM, patching and recovery. Assign evidence owners rather than treating managed services as fully outsourced security.
criterion: The responsibility matrix covers all material services and has accountable owners.
falsification: Select one managed database and ask who proves database-user review and recoverability.
required_evidence: responsibility matrix; service-owner approvals

title: Assess landing-zone design
procedure: Compare folder boundaries, production separation, centralized services and deployment ownership against the adopted enterprise foundation design. Trace an approved exception from architecture decision to resource.
criterion: Separation and centralized controls meet the documented design or have risk-accepted exceptions.
falsification: Look for a production workload in a sandbox project or inherited development administrator access.
required_evidence: architecture diagrams; design decisions; exception register

title: Review exceptions and policy ownership
procedure: Join policy overrides and IAM changes to the exception register. Verify business justification, accountable approval, expiry, compensating evidence and review dates.
criterion: Each material exception has a current owner, time limit and tested compensating control.
falsification: Find a locally overridden constraint with no current approval.
required_evidence: exception register; policy baseline; review minutes

title: Review project lifecycle and shutdown
procedure: Inspect labels, lifecycle states, enabled services and billing links. Trace creation approval, handover and one past retirement to retained evidence and revoked access.
criterion: Creation and retirement records reconcile to inventory without orphaned ownership, data or access.
falsification: Select a retired project whose data export, billing liability or service account remains unexplained.
required_evidence: creation and retirement tickets; retention approvals

title: Resolve inherited privileged access
procedure: Read organization, all ancestor folders, project and resource policies. Expand groups through authorized directory evidence and inspect custom role permissions, conditions, deny and principal boundary policies.
criterion: Each effective privileged access path is justified, assigned to an accountable identity and periodically reviewed.
falsification: A harmless-looking project policy conceals an organization-level group with broad access; trace a nested member.
required_evidence: group membership export; effective-access workpaper; access approvals
operations: org_iam; folder_iam; project_iam; asset_iam; org_roles; project_roles

title: Assess MFA and identity federation
procedure: Reconcile privileged principals with Cloud Identity, Google Workspace or workforce IdP enforcement exports. Review phishing-resistant factors, federation trust, session policy and exemptions without assuming gcloud IAM proves MFA.
criterion: Approved authentication requirements cover human privileged paths and exceptions have independent evidence.
falsification: Choose a privileged external principal excluded from the main employee MFA policy.
required_evidence: IdP policy and membership exports; authentication review

title: Review joiner mover leaver controls
procedure: Join active bindings, external principals and group membership to HR and supplier lifecycle records. Sample terminations and role changes across the review period and inspect actual removal times.
criterion: Access changes meet the company's approved service levels and retain evidence of review.
falsification: Select an offboarded contractor whose nested group still grants access.
required_evidence: HR sample; directory membership; removal tickets

title: Review emergency and time-bound privilege
procedure: Identify emergency identities, standing roles and privileged-access approval arrangements. Inspect prior emergency exercises, vault access, activation expiry and monitoring records.
criterion: Emergency access remains usable under the stated failure scenario and accountable; temporary privilege expires as designed.
falsification: Challenge an emergency account dependent on the same unavailable IdP it is intended to bypass.
required_evidence: emergency runbook; exercise record; privilege approvals

title: Assess deny and principal access boundaries
procedure: Reconcile allow bindings with explicit deny rules, exceptions, principal-set bindings and boundary enforcement versions using resource metadata and owner exports when not inventoried.
criterion: Access analysis includes applicable allow, deny and boundary effects; unsupported permission coverage is acknowledged.
falsification: Find a boundary that does not cover the permission relied on by the proposed compensating control.
required_evidence: deny and boundary policy export; principal-set membership; access analysis

title: Inventory service account ownership
procedure: Map service accounts, default identities, attached workloads and impersonation grants to owners and intended permissions. Inspect both use and administration of each identity.
criterion: Privileged machine identities have specific purposes and accountable owners; default identities receive no unexplained broad access.
falsification: A low-privileged deployer can attach or impersonate an overprivileged runtime identity.
required_evidence: service account register; application ownership; impersonation analysis

title: Review user-managed service account keys
procedure: List key metadata for every discovered service account. Reconcile key age, expiry, disabled status, owner and external storage with the approved key policy; do not read private key material.
criterion: Every user-managed key is justified and managed within the company's approved lifecycle, with a keyless migration decision.
falsification: An unused service account still has an active externally held key with no custodian.
required_evidence: key exception register; rotation records; usage review

title: Validate federation trust boundaries
procedure: Inspect workload pools and provider issuer, audience, attribute mapping and condition. Trace external subject claims to IAM grants and repository or cloud ownership.
criterion: Trust restricts intended external tenants and subjects; broad pools and impersonation grants are justified.
falsification: Test the reasoning with a forked repository or different external tenant that might satisfy a weak attribute condition; do not request tokens.
required_evidence: federation design; provider export; subject-to-role mapping

title: Inspect service account escalation paths
procedure: Review serviceAccountUser, token creation, workload deployment and project-level permissions together. Trace who can modify code running as a sensitive service identity.
criterion: Privilege reviews cover combined deployment and identity capabilities, including cross-project service accounts.
falsification: Find an identity that cannot read data directly but can deploy code as an identity that can.
required_evidence: privilege graph; deployment approvals

title: Review workload identity activity
procedure: Join historical key, impersonation and workload-owner records to bounded audit samples. Ask for longer retained exports where the collection window is insufficient.
criterion: Activity review can distinguish expected automation from unexplained identity use without treating absence of logs as inactivity.
falsification: A key appears unused only because the relevant service's Data Access logging was disabled.
required_evidence: activity review; log coverage matrix; automation schedules

title: Verify effective organization policies
procedure: Read explicit overrides and effective values for the approved constraint list on every project. Compare against the organization's adopted baseline and conditions.
criterion: Expected constraints are effective at the intended descendants; list output alone is insufficient.
falsification: A lower-level override or conditional tag changes the result for a sensitive project.
required_evidence: constraint baseline; effective-policy comparison

title: Assess domain and external sharing restrictions
procedure: Review applicable domain-restriction constraints, existing external IAM grants and exceptions. Separate prevention of new grants from historical access review.
criterion: The chosen sharing policy and actual external principals match approved collaboration needs.
falsification: An existing external grant predates a policy change and remains unexplained.
required_evidence: external-party register; sharing exceptions

title: Assess service account key guardrails
procedure: Check effective key creation and upload restrictions, default service account grant constraints and exception projects. Reconcile guardrails with existing keys.
criterion: The intended prevention policies and legacy-key cleanup are both evidenced.
falsification: Key creation is blocked but old externally stored keys remain active.
required_evidence: key policy; exception approval; legacy key inventory

title: Review resource locations and sovereignty
procedure: Map actual resource locations, backups and service-supported location constraints to contractual requirements. Identify global services and processing paths that need separate analysis.
criterion: Approved location requirements apply to the relevant resource types and operational copies; unsupported services are documented.
falsification: A primary region is approved while backups, logs or a global endpoint fall outside the reviewed requirement.
required_evidence: data-location register; contract requirements; service exceptions

title: Review custom constraints and drift
procedure: Compare current organization-policy resources with version-controlled definitions and approved change history. Inspect dry-run versus enforced state and resource-method coverage.
criterion: Guardrails relied upon by the audit are enforced for the intended operations, with reviewed changes and exceptions.
falsification: A custom rule exists only in dry-run or does not cover the update method being relied upon.
required_evidence: policy-as-code repository export; change records

title: Resolve effective firewall exposure
procedure: Review VPC rules, hierarchical policies, target tags or service accounts, priorities, direction and disabled status. Join to routes, instance interfaces and approved service exposure.
criterion: Public and lateral paths are justified after effective rule evaluation; a single broad rule is a review candidate, not automatic proof of reachability.
falsification: A deny is shadowed by a higher-priority allow, or an apparent allow targets no instances.
required_evidence: effective-firewall export; network exposure register
operations: firewalls; firewall_policies; networks; subnets; instances; routes

title: Assess external application protection
procedure: Map external forwarding rules to backend services and Cloud Armor policy attachment. Review rule action, preview mode, bypass endpoints, TLS configuration and owner-approved exposure.
criterion: Each critical public service has the agreed protections on its actual serving path.
falsification: A protective policy exists but is unattached or all material rules run in preview.
required_evidence: load-balancer architecture; TLS policy export; exception register

title: Inspect private access and egress
procedure: Inspect subnet private access, NAT configuration, routes, service endpoints and DNS resolution design. Reconcile permitted outbound destinations with application requirements.
criterion: Private access and egress controls match the approved traffic model and observable flows.
falsification: A private VM reaches an unintended destination through NAT or a transit route.
required_evidence: egress policy; flow-log analysis; network diagrams

title: Assess VPC Service Controls
procedure: Read access policies and perimeter status, ingress, egress, restricted services, access levels and dry-run specifications. Reconcile perimeter project numbers and bridges to data flows.
criterion: The perimeter protects the intended supported services and approved cross-boundary paths in enforced configuration.
falsification: A protected project has an unrestricted service path, bridge or broad ingress identity condition.
required_evidence: perimeter design; access-level export; dry-run review

title: Review DNS and network telemetry
procedure: Review DNS zone visibility and DNSSEC where applicable, flow-log enablement and firewall logging on material paths. Obtain existing queries or flow samples and retention evidence.
criterion: Telemetry supports the agreed detection use cases; name resolution and DNS change ownership are controlled.
falsification: A critical subnet or deny rule has no logging while a dashboard suggests complete network visibility.
required_evidence: DNS settings export; flow evidence; network monitoring use cases

title: Review Shared VPC administration
procedure: Identify host and service projects and network-user grants. Reconcile cross-project service identities and ownership of firewall, subnet and DNS changes.
criterion: Host and service project responsibilities and permissions preserve the approved separation.
falsification: A service-project deployer can alter shared host-network security unexpectedly.
required_evidence: Shared VPC relationship export; responsibility matrix

title: Assess VPN redundancy and authentication
procedure: Inspect VPN tunnels, peer endpoints, routing and status evidence against the intended availability design. Review key custody from records without retrieving preshared secrets.
criterion: Redundancy and routing match the approved design, with current monitoring and prior failure-test evidence.
falsification: Two apparently redundant tunnels depend on the same unprotected peer device or connection.
required_evidence: VPN topology; key custody record; prior failover results

title: Assess Interconnect dependencies
procedure: Map attachments, edge locations, router peers and provider circuits to business-critical paths. Review utilization and fault evidence from existing monitoring exports.
criterion: Availability objectives account for provider, facility and routing dependencies.
falsification: Nominally redundant attachments share a failure domain omitted from the design.
required_evidence: provider circuit records; monitoring export; topology

title: Review peering and transit trust
procedure: Review peering, imported and exported routes, custom routes and network connectivity hubs found in asset metadata. Trace intended access across shared or acquired organizations.
criterion: Each trust connection has an owner, purpose and reviewed reachability analysis.
falsification: A new peering or exported default route extends access beyond the approved boundary.
required_evidence: peering approvals; transit routing analysis

title: Assess hybrid administration access
procedure: Trace SSH, RDP and administrative application access through IAP, VPN or equivalent controls. Review IAM conditions, instance login controls and existing access logs.
criterion: Administrative access meets approved identity and network requirements, including emergency paths.
falsification: An external address and permissive rule bypass the documented administrative gateway.
required_evidence: administration design; IAP access policy export; access sample

title: Review VM identity and metadata
procedure: Inspect instance service accounts, access scopes, project and instance metadata, external addresses and sensitive startup configuration. Reconcile identity purpose with IAM privileges.
criterion: Runtime identity and metadata follow the approved baseline; exported values are handled as sensitive.
falsification: A VM uses a default overprivileged identity or a project SSH key unexpectedly applies.
required_evidence: VM baseline; identity mapping; metadata review

title: Assess host login controls
procedure: Inspect OS Login metadata and exceptions, project-wide SSH keys, IAP path and administrative roles. Use guest-side authorized evidence for local accounts not represented in GCP APIs.
criterion: All privileged host access paths are covered by current identity, MFA and lifecycle requirements.
falsification: A compliant OS Login setting coexists with an unmanaged local administrator account.
required_evidence: guest account inventory; login policy; access review

title: Review boot integrity and images
procedure: Inspect Shielded VM settings, image origin, image lifecycle and approved exceptions. Correlate vulnerability and configuration records for the operating system.
criterion: Image provenance and boot controls meet the adopted platform baseline.
falsification: A production image is outside the approved pipeline or an integrity exception has no owner.
required_evidence: image approval; integrity monitoring; vulnerability export

title: Assess patching and vulnerability operations
procedure: Reconcile OS inventory and vulnerability or patch-management exports to the VM population. Sample overdue fixes, maintenance approvals and validated exceptions.
criterion: The approved remediation timelines are met across the entire VM population, including unmanaged hosts.
falsification: A healthy patch dashboard excludes an instance with no inventory agent.
required_evidence: patch compliance export; asset reconciliation; exception records

title: Inspect disks and deletion protection
procedure: Review disk encryption references, attachment, snapshot schedules and instance deletion protection where applicable. Join backup coverage to business recovery requirements.
criterion: Data-bearing compute resources have approved protection, encryption and recovery arrangements.
falsification: An unattached sensitive disk or critical instance lacks the expected backup association.
required_evidence: disk classification; backup mapping; deletion policy

title: Assess cluster control-plane access
procedure: Inspect cluster endpoint exposure, authorized networks, IAM integration and authentication settings. Reconcile private connectivity and administrator paths.
criterion: Control-plane access matches the documented threat model and approved administrator population.
falsification: A private-node cluster still has an unintended public control-plane access path.
required_evidence: cluster architecture; administrator review

title: Review Kubernetes RBAC and admission
procedure: Use cluster configuration plus customer-provided metadata exports of roles, bindings, admission policies and workloads. Trace namespace administrators and cluster-wide privilege without reading Kubernetes Secret payloads.
criterion: RBAC and admission enforcement constrain the intended workloads and administrators.
falsification: A namespace owner can create a privileged workload or bind an unintended cluster role.
required_evidence: Kubernetes RBAC export; admission policy and results; namespace ownership

title: Assess workload and node identity
procedure: Inspect Workload Identity Federation settings, node service accounts and metadata protection. Trace Kubernetes service-account identity grants to Google APIs.
criterion: Workloads have appropriately scoped identities and cannot rely on unnecessarily privileged node credentials.
falsification: A workload without its own grant can obtain access through an excessive node identity or deployment permission.
required_evidence: Kubernetes service-account mapping; node identity review

title: Review cluster maintenance and supply chain
procedure: Inspect versions, release channels, maintenance exclusions and node update policy. Reconcile image admission, vulnerability evidence and supported-version requirements.
criterion: The cluster and node population follows an approved support and upgrade policy with controlled exclusions.
falsification: An apparently current control plane masks old nodes or a long-lived maintenance exclusion.
required_evidence: version inventory; upgrade history; image provenance

title: Assess workload isolation and recovery
procedure: Inspect dataplane, network-policy and backup configuration; obtain actual policy coverage, persistent-volume mapping and past restore results. Treat Autopilot and Standard responsibilities separately.
criterion: Isolation and recovery requirements are evidenced at workload level, including persistent state.
falsification: A network-policy capability is enabled but a sensitive namespace has no effective policy, or its volumes are outside backup scope.
required_evidence: network-policy export; volume inventory; restore report

title: Review Cloud Run exposure and identity
procedure: Inspect service ingress, revision configuration, authentication/IAM and runtime identities across all approved regions. Review direct service URLs and load-balancer paths together.
criterion: Public invocation and runtime privileges match the application's approved exposure.
falsification: A load balancer is protected while the underlying service remains invokable directly.
required_evidence: service architecture; invoker review; region inventory

title: Assess functions and event triggers
procedure: Map functions to generation, runtime identity, ingress and event sources. Reconcile source ownership, authentication and supported runtime lifecycle.
criterion: Each function and trigger has controlled invocation and maintained runtime dependencies.
falsification: An event path or old function generation is omitted from the application inventory.
required_evidence: function inventory; trigger policy; runtime review

title: Inspect scheduled and batch execution
procedure: Review Cloud Run jobs and Scheduler targets, service identities and authorization. Check whether embedded request bodies, arguments or environment values contain sensitive material.
criterion: Automated jobs have least-privileged identities, reviewed destinations and failure handling.
falsification: A scheduler can call an unintended authenticated endpoint or silently fails without owner response.
required_evidence: job ownership; failure records; target authorization

title: Review messaging access and data lifecycle
procedure: Inspect topic and subscription IAM, push authentication, retention, dead-letter configuration and encryption references. Reconcile subscriber destinations and data sensitivity.
criterion: Authorized publishers and subscribers, retention and delivery behavior match the approved data flow.
falsification: An external push endpoint or dead-letter topic retains sensitive data outside the documented boundary.
required_evidence: messaging data flow; subscriber ownership; retention approval

title: Assess runtime secrets and network dependencies
procedure: Inspect revision metadata, secret references, VPC connectivity and egress configuration. Obtain deployment records and existing health evidence without invoking workloads.
criterion: Runtime dependencies, secret versions and network access follow the deployment baseline.
falsification: A new revision uses an unreviewed secret version or broad egress and remains outside the operating review.
required_evidence: deployment history; secret mapping; dependency diagram

title: Assess public and external bucket access
procedure: Join bucket metadata, IAM bindings, inherited public access prevention and approved external-sharing uses. If uniform access is off, request object ACL metadata separately; do not download objects.
criterion: Public and external access is intentional and governed across IAM, ACL and signed-access paths.
falsification: Public prevention is enabled but long-lived signed URLs or legacy object ACL exposure are absent from the review.
required_evidence: sharing register; ACL metadata when applicable; signed URL governance

title: Review uniform access and granular permissions
procedure: Inspect uniform bucket-level access, managed folders and resource IAM. Reconcile legacy bucket and object ACLs where uniform access is disabled.
criterion: The actual permission system is covered by the access review, including managed folders.
falsification: A project-level review overlooks a bucket or managed-folder grant, or assumes IAM describes every object ACL.
required_evidence: bucket permission review; managed-folder inventory; legacy ACL export

title: Assess retention lifecycle and deletion recovery
procedure: Review retention policy, lock status, lifecycle rules, versioning and soft-delete settings against approved retention and recovery requirements.
criterion: Retention and deletion recovery work together with legal requirements and operational needs; locks are assessed without changing them.
falsification: A lifecycle action removes recoverable versions before the required recovery window.
required_evidence: retention schedule; legal holds; recovery examples

title: Inspect bucket encryption and location
procedure: Map storage location, default key references and object-encryption evidence to requirements. A default CMEK setting alone does not prove all existing objects use that key.
criterion: Location and encryption requirements are supported for current and historical data populations.
falsification: An object predates the default key change or a key's location conflicts with the assumed recovery design.
required_evidence: encryption coverage export; location requirements; key dependency map

title: Review storage logging and transfer paths
procedure: Reconcile Data Access settings, bucket access patterns, storage-transfer resources and owner-provided transfer histories. Inspect service-agent permissions and external destinations.
criterion: Material reads and transfers have the agreed authorization, telemetry and retention coverage.
falsification: An apparently inactive public object path produces no authenticated access log and is misclassified as unused.
required_evidence: transfer-job export; access review; logging coverage

title: Review Cloud SQL access and exposure
procedure: Inspect public and private addresses, authorized networks, TLS requirements, flags and IAM database authentication. Request database-native user and grant evidence; project IAM is only part of the review.
criterion: Network paths and database identities meet the approved access model for each engine.
falsification: A private instance has an unmanaged database administrator or a TLS mode weaker than the documented baseline.
required_evidence: database user and grant export; connectivity design; engine baseline

title: Assess SQL availability and recovery
procedure: Inspect availability type, backups, point-in-time recovery and replica configuration for the actual database engine. Review past restore records and dependent encryption keys.
criterion: The selected configuration and demonstrated restore capability meet approved RPO and RTO.
falsification: A successful backup exists but point-in-time recovery is unavailable for the incident window.
required_evidence: recovery objectives; backup history; restore results

title: Review BigQuery access and fine-grained controls
procedure: Use dataset and table asset metadata plus approved exports of row policies, policy tags, masking rules and authorized views. Trace inherited IAM, dataset ACLs and data-sharing links.
criterion: Sensitive data access is justified at dataset, table, row and column levels where required; metadata-only coverage is documented.
falsification: An authorized view or broad dataset grant bypasses the intended interpretation of a masking control.
required_evidence: dataset ACL export; row and column policy metadata; sharing register

title: Assess BigQuery lifecycle and query governance
procedure: Inspect dataset locations, encryption, expirations, reservations and job-history evidence supplied by owners. Review copies, extracts and scheduled transfers without running SQL jobs.
criterion: Retention, processing locations and query/export use match approved data and cost policies.
falsification: A dataset expiry looks compliant while extracted tables persist in another project or bucket.
required_evidence: job-history metadata; transfer schedules; data retention matrix

title: Assess other managed data platforms
procedure: Identify Spanner, Firestore, Bigtable, AlloyDB, Redis and data-processing services from inventory. Apply service-specific access, network, encryption, availability and backup tests using owner-provided metadata where native collectors are absent.
criterion: Every material data platform has an explicit evidence plan; absence of a dedicated collector is not treated as absence of risk.
falsification: A critical Firestore or Bigtable service is omitted because only SQL instances were enumerated.
required_evidence: service-specific configuration exports; native grants; restore evidence

title: Review Secret Manager access and replication
procedure: Inspect secret metadata, replication, IAM, labels and owners. Trace read and administration privileges while never accessing secret payloads.
criterion: Secret access and location are justified and match the documented consuming workloads.
falsification: A broad project-level Secret Accessor grant exposes unrelated application secrets.
required_evidence: secret ownership; consumer mapping; access review

title: Assess secret rotation and version lifecycle
procedure: List version metadata, status and dates; inspect rotation notifications, automation records and deployment version references. A rotation schedule is not proof the secret changed.
criterion: Rotation and revocation operate within approved requirements and applications consume intended versions.
falsification: A configured rotation topic has no functioning subscriber or workloads still use an old enabled version.
required_evidence: rotation execution records; version-to-deployment mapping

title: Assess KMS purpose and separation of duties
procedure: Inspect key rings, algorithms, protection level, IAM and encrypt/decrypt versus administration permissions. Map key projects and service agents to protected resources.
criterion: Key administration and use align with the approved custody and separation model.
falsification: A data administrator can also grant themselves decryption access to the same sensitive dataset.
required_evidence: key inventory; custody matrix; access review

title: Review key lifecycle and availability
procedure: Review primary versions, rotation and destruction schedule evidence. Reconcile disabled or pending-destruction versions with active data and backup dependencies.
criterion: Key lifecycle changes preserve required availability and approved cryptographic policy.
falsification: A retained backup depends on a key version scheduled for destruction before retention ends.
required_evidence: key-version metadata export; destruction approvals; dependency mapping

title: Assess CMEK and external key dependencies
procedure: Map required CMEK coverage and EKM or HSM requirements to actual resource metadata and service support. Review provider outages, key access and previous recovery evidence.
criterion: The adopted encryption model is implemented where required and its operational dependencies are understood.
falsification: A CMEK label is present while the service resource uses provider-managed encryption, or EKM recovery is untested.
required_evidence: CMEK coverage matrix; external-key contract; recovery evidence

title: Verify Data Access audit coverage
procedure: Read organization, ancestor-folder and project auditConfigs, service exceptions and exempted principals. Map enabled services to the required ADMIN_READ, DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE coverage.
criterion: The adopted logging matrix is effectively configured and inherited exemptions are explicitly reviewed.
falsification: An empty project auditConfig is interpreted without inspecting inherited settings, or an exemption suppresses the chosen principal.
required_evidence: service logging matrix; effective auditConfig analysis

title: Review routing sinks and exclusions
procedure: Inspect project and organization sinks, inclusion and exclusion filters, destination ownership and writer grants. Review intercepting behavior and aggregated child scope.
criterion: Required events reach approved destinations without unintended filtering or privilege gaps.
falsification: A central sink exists but its writer lacks destination access or its filter excludes the target event.
required_evidence: sink destination IAM; delivery metrics; filter review

title: Assess retention location and protected access
procedure: Inspect log bucket retention, location, access restrictions and lock state across all used locations. Reconcile SIEM and archive retention outside Cloud Logging.
criterion: The retention and access model satisfies the adopted evidence requirements across every copy.
falsification: Only global buckets were checked while a regional bucket holds the relevant events for a shorter period.
required_evidence: retention matrix; SIEM settings; bucket access review

title: Prove an existing event's end-to-end trace
procedure: Select a known historical approved administrative or data event from a ticket. Trace it through source logging, sink routing, destination and detection within a bounded UTC window.
criterion: The specific event is attributable and retrievable with expected fields and timing; the sample's limits are documented.
falsification: The source event is present but disappears after routing, or the sampled log window omits the ticket time.
required_evidence: known-event record; source and destination evidence; timing comparison

title: Assess integrity and evidence visibility
procedure: Review log administration, private-log viewing, deletion and sink modification privileges. Reconcile coverage counts and missing-access errors before concluding about activity.
criterion: The audit can explain who can read or affect evidence and where visibility is incomplete.
falsification: The collector receives no private entries because it lacks Private Logs Viewer permissions.
required_evidence: evidence-access matrix; error register; log administrator review

title: Assess Security Command Center coverage
procedure: Reconcile activation scope, edition, data location, services, detectors and project population with expected coverage. Read findings and record activation or permission failures.
criterion: Finding absence is interpreted only after coverage is demonstrated; tier-dependent gaps have compensating evidence.
falsification: An empty finding list comes from a location without the organization's findings or a disabled detector.
required_evidence: SCC configuration export; coverage matrix; detector status

title: Review finding triage and suppression
procedure: Sample active findings, muted records and ticket links. Evaluate severity, exploitability, asset criticality, owner, age and suppression justification.
criterion: Material findings receive timely owned decisions under approved response targets.
falsification: A long-lived mute hides a recurring public exposure with no expiry or risk acceptance.
required_evidence: triage queue; mute rules; ticket samples

title: Validate detection use cases
procedure: Map priority threats to required logs, analytics, alert routes and past incident or exercise records. Inspect existing test results rather than injecting attacks.
criterion: The agreed use cases have demonstrated signal delivery and response evidence.
falsification: A detection rule is enabled but depends on a disabled Data Access log source.
required_evidence: detection catalog; prior exercise results; alert routing export

title: Assess incident readiness and containment authority
procedure: Review contacts, evidence preservation, organization access, service-account revocation and network isolation procedures. Compare responsibilities against a previous incident or tabletop.
criterion: Responders can identify authorized decision makers and required access during the stated scenario.
falsification: A responder's emergency credentials depend on the affected identity service or cannot access the evidence project.
required_evidence: incident plan; contact roster; tabletop report

title: Review incident lessons and closure
procedure: Trace a sample of historical incidents through scope, root-cause evidence, notification decisions and verified corrective actions. Compare recurring SCC findings and logs.
criterion: Closure includes validation of the failed control and documented residual risk.
falsification: A closed incident recurs with the same underlying access path.
required_evidence: incident sample; postmortems; closure evidence

title: Map recovery objectives to dependencies
procedure: Join critical services to data stores, identities, keys, DNS, networking and provider dependencies. Obtain business-approved RPO and RTO, including data-loss tolerance.
criterion: Recovery objectives cover the complete service chain and have accountable owners.
falsification: A database meets its RTO while identity or DNS recovery prevents the business application from operating.
required_evidence: business impact analysis; dependency map; approved RPO/RTO

title: Review backup coverage and immutability
procedure: Reconcile data-bearing resources with snapshot, SQL backup, GKE backup and Backup and DR metadata. Inspect retention, separation, vault protection and administration.
criterion: All required data has a mapped backup mechanism and approved protection from common administrative failure.
falsification: The same compromised administrator can erase production data and every retained backup.
required_evidence: backup coverage matrix; vault settings export; administrator review

title: Assess restore evidence
procedure: Read existing backup metadata and hash supplied prior restore reports. Review restored scope, timestamp, data integrity checks, elapsed time and business acceptance.
criterion: Prior restore evidence demonstrates the agreed objective for the sampled system; missing exercises remain a gap.
falsification: A report says successful but omits application integrity checks or restores only an empty database.
required_evidence: dated restore reports; integrity checks; business sign-off

title: Review regional and zonal failure readiness
procedure: Inspect multi-zone or regional configurations and compare capacity, quotas and dependencies to the failover design. Evaluate existing exercises and their assumptions.
criterion: The adopted failure scenario is covered by realistic capacity and independent dependencies.
falsification: A secondary region shares a key, network or quota bottleneck that prevents recovery.
required_evidence: failover design; capacity evidence; prior exercise

title: Assess recovery operations and ownership
procedure: Review recovery runbooks, access prerequisites, communications and retrospective improvements. Verify named owners can locate retained evidence and necessary approvals.
criterion: Runbooks remain usable under the scenario and material exercise findings are resolved or accepted.
falsification: An offline recovery step requires a console or repository available only in the failed environment.
required_evidence: runbook review; access checklist; exercise action log

title: Review source and build trigger trust
procedure: Inspect Cloud Build triggers, event filters, approval settings, repository connections and execution identities. Reconcile branch protection and contributor permissions from the source platform.
criterion: Untrusted changes cannot silently obtain production deployment authority through the approved pipeline.
falsification: A pull request can edit the pipeline that runs with a production service account.
required_evidence: repository protection export; pipeline design; trigger approvals

title: Assess build identity and secrets
procedure: Review build service accounts, worker pools, network access and secret references. Inspect a bounded sample of historical builds without triggering builds.
criterion: Build privileges and secret availability are appropriate to repository trust and deployment purpose.
falsification: An untrusted build can impersonate the same identity that deploys production.
required_evidence: build configuration export; secret mapping; identity review

title: Review artifact access and vulnerability governance
procedure: Inspect repository locations, format, IAM and cleanup policies; obtain scan status, SBOM and exception evidence for deployed digests.
criterion: Deployed artifacts have attributable provenance and reviewed vulnerabilities under the adopted policy.
falsification: A clean repository summary excludes the exact digest running in production.
required_evidence: deployed digest register; scan export; SBOM; exceptions

title: Assess deployment approvals and admission
procedure: Inspect delivery pipelines, Binary Authorization policy and approved attestor evidence. Trace one deployed artifact to source, build, approval and admission result.
criterion: Production admission and approval requirements are effective, with controlled break-glass use.
falsification: Policy exists but enforcement permits all images or a production target bypasses the pipeline.
required_evidence: release sample; attestation metadata; admission results

title: Review infrastructure drift and change evidence
procedure: Compare current resource exports with approved infrastructure-as-code state and change records. Trace risky IAM, firewall and policy changes in the audit sample.
criterion: Material drift is identified, owned and reconciled to approved changes.
falsification: A console change weakens a guardrail while the repository still shows the compliant setting.
required_evidence: IaC export; drift report; change sample

title: Inventory AI services and accountable uses
owner: AI platform and data governance leads
procedure: Inventory Vertex AI endpoints, models and datasets across approved regions; reconcile managed generative services, agent runtimes and external model integrations from application records.
criterion: All material AI uses have owners, data classifications, model/provider records and approved purposes.
falsification: An application calls a managed model API without a dedicated endpoint and is missed by endpoint inventory.
required_evidence: AI use-case register; provider inventory; application data flow

title: Assess AI data use and retention
owner: AI platform and data governance leads
procedure: Review model-specific data governance, prompt logging, grounding, caches, tuning data and retention settings against the actual contract and feature. Do not equate training restrictions with zero retention.
criterion: Approved data handling addresses each enabled feature and provider, with documented exceptions.
falsification: A zero-retention assertion overlooks grounding, abuse-monitoring or optional logging behavior.
required_evidence: feature and retention matrix; contracts; data approvals

title: Review AI endpoint and runtime access
owner: AI platform and data governance leads
procedure: Inspect endpoint networking, IAM, service identities, keys and data-store permissions. Reconcile who can deploy, invoke, tune or change the runtime.
criterion: AI service privilege and exposure match the approved use and sensitive-data boundary.
falsification: An endpoint deployer can substitute a model that runs under a more privileged identity.
required_evidence: AI access review; endpoint architecture; runtime identity mapping

title: Assess agent tools and retrieval boundaries
owner: AI platform and data governance leads
procedure: Use application-supplied agent manifests, tool definitions, retrieval ACL design and existing evaluation traces. Review delegated identity and approval of consequential actions without invoking tools.
criterion: Agents enforce user-specific data access and approved tool authority at execution time.
falsification: A prompt or retrieved document can cause a tool to access another user's data or perform an unapproved action.
required_evidence: agent tool inventory; retrieval ACL evidence; prior adversarial evaluations

title: Review AI evaluation and operational oversight
owner: AI platform and data governance leads
procedure: Inspect model/version approvals, evaluation criteria, safety filters, monitoring, rollback and incident records. Sample completed evaluations for representative failure modes.
criterion: The production use has approved quality, safety and security acceptance criteria plus monitored failure handling.
falsification: A model passes generic quality tests but fails the business's sensitive-data or tool-authorization scenarios.
required_evidence: evaluation reports; model approvals; AI incident records

title: Assess observability against service objectives
procedure: Join workload inventory to approved SLIs, SLOs, dashboards, alerts and escalation owners from monitoring exports. Review existing incidents and error budgets.
criterion: Critical user journeys have measurable objectives and actionable monitoring.
falsification: An infrastructure dashboard is green while the business transaction is unavailable.
required_evidence: SLO register; monitoring policy export; incident sample

title: Review quotas and capacity risk
procedure: Inspect project quotas and obtain service-specific regional quota and utilization exports. Compare peak, growth and failover requirements to available headroom.
criterion: Approved capacity scenarios are covered by current quota and realistic resource availability.
falsification: A failover region has nominal architecture support but insufficient quota or capacity reservations.
required_evidence: quota register; utilization evidence; capacity plan

title: Assess maintenance and support lifecycle
procedure: Reconcile service versions, runtimes, release channels and dependencies to supported lifecycles. Review maintenance exclusions, support plans and upgrade ownership.
criterion: Unsupported or soon-retiring dependencies have an approved transition or exception.
falsification: A function runtime or GKE node pool remains unsupported despite a maintained application repository.
required_evidence: support matrix; upgrade plan; provider notices

title: Review operational change and access
procedure: Trace sampled production changes to approvals, tests, deployment records and post-change verification. Include emergency changes and supplier access.
criterion: Changes have accountable authorization and sufficient validation for their risk.
falsification: A sensitive console change bypassed normal deployment approval without emergency review.
required_evidence: change samples; emergency approvals; supplier access review

title: Assess service ownership and incident learning
procedure: Reconcile ownership labels and on-call records with real responders, dependency owners and postmortem actions.
criterion: Critical services have current operational owners and improvements tied to recurring failure modes.
falsification: A labeled owner has left or a repeated failure has no tracked corrective action.
required_evidence: service catalog; on-call roster; postmortem actions

title: Reconcile billing and project accountability
procedure: Read billing associations for approved projects and compare with finance-approved account and cost-center records. Billing account scope requires explicit independent approval.
criterion: Every billed project has an accountable owner, cost center and approved billing association.
falsification: A project absent from the operations register still produces charges.
required_evidence: finance project register; billing account approvals; cost allocation

title: Review budgets and spend control behavior
procedure: Inspect budgets for explicitly approved accounts, filters, thresholds and recipients. Determine whether a budget is alerts-only or a supported spend-cap configuration and inspect actual handling.
criterion: Budget behavior and alert response match the adopted cost-control requirement; no generic assumption that every budget caps spending.
falsification: An alerts-only threshold is mistaken for an enforced stop, or notification reaches an unattended mailbox.
required_evidence: budget approvals; notification delivery; response records

title: Assess allocation and cost reporting
procedure: Reconcile labels and tags to approved allocation rules and existing billing-export configuration. Request owner-supplied query results; do not submit BigQuery jobs from the collector.
criterion: Material costs can be assigned and reconciled with finance at the agreed level.
falsification: Unlabeled shared infrastructure or credits distort the reported cost allocation.
required_evidence: billing-export settings; allocation report; finance reconciliation

title: Review optimization decisions and commitments
procedure: Compare idle resource and utilization evidence with existing recommendations, commitments and business demand. Validate savings assumptions and contractual terms with finance.
criterion: Optimization recommendations account for reliability, commitment coverage and real workload demand.
falsification: An idle-looking disaster recovery resource is proposed for removal without its recovery role.
required_evidence: utilization report; recommendation export; commitment register

title: Assess cost anomalies and abuse readiness
procedure: Correlate spending anomalies, identity activity and public exposure with approved workloads. Review response authority and previous cost incidents.
criterion: Unexpected spend has a defined detection and response path with accountable decisions.
falsification: A compromised workload can consume large resources before anyone acts on the cost alert.
required_evidence: anomaly history; cost response procedure; incident sample

title: Map obligations to system scope
procedure: Identify applicable contracts, jurisdictional requirements and adopted frameworks with the organization. Map obligations to services, data, controls and evidence owners rather than assuming provider certification transfers.
criterion: Every adopted requirement has an applicability decision and evidence mapping approved by the accountable team.
falsification: A provider attestation is offered as proof that customer IAM or retention configuration complies.
required_evidence: obligation register; scope decisions; control crosswalk

title: Assess classification and data discovery
procedure: Compare data classification and existing discovery/profile results with storage, databases, datasets and AI inventories. Inspect coverage, location, job recency and exclusions without initiating scans.
criterion: Classification covers the material data population, with explicit unsupported or unscanned areas.
falsification: A current discovery dashboard excludes a new project, unstructured store or encrypted dataset.
required_evidence: classification register; discovery profile export; coverage reconciliation

title: Review privacy lifecycle and deletion evidence
procedure: Trace selected data flows through collection, purpose, sharing, retention, deletion and backups using owner-provided records. Resolve legal hold and recovery obligations with the accountable team.
criterion: The adopted privacy requirements are supported across copies and processors; technical settings alone do not prove legal compliance.
falsification: A deleted primary record persists in extracts, logs or a downstream AI dataset without an approved retention basis.
required_evidence: data-flow map; deletion request samples; processor register

title: Assess regulated workload controls
procedure: Identify Assured Workloads, access approvals, transparency logs, regional restrictions and contractual support commitments where applicable. Inspect actual control package and exceptions.
criterion: Claims about sovereign or regulated operation match deployed controls, service eligibility and contract terms.
falsification: A project label claims a regulated package while the workload or service is outside its supported boundary.
required_evidence: control-package export; contracts; access approval records

title: Review audit evidence and assurance closure
procedure: Check findings against criteria, affected population, reproducible evidence and contrary explanations. Require owners, agreed actions, due dates, risk acceptance and independent retest before closure.
criterion: The report distinguishes observed facts, inference, limitations and management decisions; no unsupported compliance claim remains.
falsification: A high-severity finding relies on truncated data or is marked closed after a change ticket without retest evidence.
required_evidence: finding register; quality review; management responses; closure evidence
